title: Cap. III Sol. Rat. 14: same execution order granted — opposite order of intention denied
pass_a_gloss: We grant therefore that God in the same order in which in time he puts things into execution decreed from eternity and foresaw that they would be put: but we deny that in the order in which he puts into execution, or decreed to put, he also intended. For since in the acts of the Divine will and mind there is of themselves no priority or posteriority of order, according to our mode of understanding and the relation of the things themselves, not the same but a plainly opposite order is to be conceived in Divine execution and intention. The decree of execution always begins from that which is more remote from the end itself, and so progresses step by step to the effecting of the end: in this sense; God decreed to call Paul before justifying, to justify and adorn with good works before glorifying. For since the decree of execution, or executive will, regards the external and actual effecting of the thing, that must be referred earlier to this will which earlier concurs to effecting the thing. But now on the contrary, the intention of the will always begins from the end itself, and from the end so progresses to the means that it always wills earlier that which is nearer the end.
pass_b_english: So we grant God decreed from eternity and foresaw that things would be executed in the same order he executes them in time — but we deny he also intended in that execution-order. In the acts of the divine will and mind there is of themselves no priority of order; on our way of understanding and the things' relation, execution and intention take plainly opposite orders. The decree of execution always starts from what is farther from the end and steps toward effecting it: God decreed to call Paul before justifying him, to justify and adorn with good works before glorifying. Executive will regards the external actual effecting, so what concurs earlier to producing the thing is referred earlier to that will. Intention, conversely, always starts from the end itself and moves to means so that it always wills first what is nearer the end.
source_text: Damus ergo, Deum eodem ordine quo in tempore mandat res exsecutioni, decrevisse ab aeterno et praevidisse quod mandarentur: sed negamus, eo ordine quo mandat exsecutioni, aut decrevit mandare, etiam intendisse. Nam cum in actibus voluntatis et mentis Divinae per se nulla sit prioritas aut posterioritas ordinis, secundum nostrum modum intelligendi, et rerum ipsarum habitudinem, non idem, sed plane oppositus ordo concipiendus est in exsecutione atque intentione Divina. Decretum exsecutionis orditur semper ab eo quod est remotius ab ipso fine, et sic gradatim progreditur ad effectionem finis: hoc sensu; Deus decrevit vocare Paulum prius quam justificare, justificare et bonis operibus ornare prius quam glorificare. Cum enim decretum exsecutionis, vel voluntas exsecutiva respiciat externam et actualem rei effectionem, illud prius ad hanc voluntatem referatur necesse est quod prius concurrit ad rem efficiendam. Jam vero e contra, Intentio voluntatis orditur semper ab ipso fine, et a fine sic ad media progreditur, ut semper prius id velit quod est fini propinquius.
